items.name: cipher_rt_fp8_engine.cpp — cuBLASLt per-tensor scalar E4M3 engine
items.detail: What it substitutes: per-tensor scalar FP8 E4M3 GEMM via cublasLtMatmul — ':5-8 Per-tensor scalar FP8 E4M3 (the ONLY fused path on this cu13 cuBLASLt — rowwise NOT_SUPPORTED, measured 2026-05-30). Static per-tensor weight prequant (one-time, cached by w_ptr) + inline per-tensor activation quant + cuBLASLt FP8 scalar GEMM (FAST_ACCUM) -> fp16/bf16 output DIRECTLY (no epilogue)'. Matmul desc: TRANSA=T/TRANSB=N, FAST_ACCUM=1, COMPUTE_32F, A/B scale pointers set per call, 32MB workspace, heuristic algo cached per (m,n,k,dtype) shape (:298-316, :334-338, :115). Quant kernels (absmax reduce + clamp-to-±448 quantize, fp16+bf16 variants) are NVRTC-compiled at runtime and launched via driver cuLaunchKernel, explicitly NOT static .cu, to avoid SIGFPE through CIPHER's own __cudaRegisterFunction intercept at LD_PRELOAD time (:10-15, :40-73, :180-212). All cuBLASLt/driver/NVRTC symbols resolved by dlsym from libcublasLt.so.13/.12, libcuda.so.1, libnvrtc.so.13/.12 (:146-152). Opt-in single-entry shared-activation-quant cache for q/k/v and gate/up reuse, env CIPHER_FP8_SHARE_ACT (:134-144, :175, :321-330); NVRTC include override env CIPHER_FP8_CUDA_INC (:186-188).

inventory.summary: TOPIC A: Marlin is an INT4 (group-128) weight-quantized GEMM substitution actuator on the cublasGemmEx dispatch substrate, gated to decode-shaped GEMMs (batch M<=64, N>=1024, K>=1024, K%128==0, N%64==0), armed by env CIPHER_MARLIN + classifier marlin_engage + TLS dispatch hint, with lazy quantize after 4 observations. It substitutes fp16 GEMMs directly and bf16 GEMMs via a cast-to-fp16 surrogate into the NVRTC-compiled IST-DASLab Marlin kernel (10 entry points, grid=SM count, 96KB dyn smem). Prior results located: V0 scorecard 'Marlin 3600 + FP8 1125 = 4725 of the 4725 routed GEMMs' (bf16_observed=4950, substituted=3600, weights_q=225) in a FORCE-ARMED eager Phase D pass; NF4 co-fire ~5.6GB/7B (single-model LIVE reading 5.5GB) is a separate transformers/bitsandbytes path with no .so counter. Marlin is a BYTES/token (bandwidth-reduction) lever per the MFU dossier's own words; no report claims an MFU% lift from Marlin (its committed number is 1.38x tok/s at B=8 from may13). Marlin was NOT engaged in the V1 production router (agent=engine+DVFS+NF4, compute=FP8; CIPHER_MARLIN never set to 1, explicitly 0 in the OFF-proof and V2 deb gates; classifier policy for A4_BATCH_INFERENCE gates marlin_engage=0; capture-illegal inside the engine graph). One report-vs-source naming discrepancy: scorecard says 'bf16->Machete' but the source substitutes into the Marlin INT4 NVRTC kernel; the Machete intercept is count-and-forward passthrough whose g_machete_substituted counter is never incremented. TOPIC B: Koopman is a rank-r EDMD surrogate actuator (shipped kernel hard-coded FP16_R=64) replacing FP16 GEMMs for registry-calibrated shapes, behind an OOD gate beta=0.05 (default) computed by cipher_koopman_fp16_ood_max_residual. Reports confirm: live OOD residual 0.91-0.97 >> 0.05 so it never fires; shipped .cu kernel measured 0.04x/0.05x = 25x/20x SLOWER than the cuBLAS GEMM it replaces; '7.43x LM-head' and 'rank ~1773' both phantoms (no provenance, do not reproduce); activation effective rank 844-2630 of 4096 makes r=64 ~13-40x too small; output-residual accuracy floor ~0.25 (never <0.08) flat r=16..r=64. Verdict: built-but-(correctly)-never-fires, and it could not lift MFU even if it worked — it is a FLOP-REDUCTION lever (replaces K*N FLOPs/row with r*(K+N)+r^2), i.e., a metric mismatch with MFU: at ranks where any speedup survives quality is destroyed, at quality-surviving rank (~2048) the FLOP ceiling is only 1.8x, and the low-rank surrogate is a skinny memory-bound op that would LOWER silicon FLOP utilization; the realized kernel is a 20-25x slowdown besides.

items.name: B-verdict: Koopman could NOT lift MFU even if it fired — metric mismatch
items.detail: Mechanism mismatch: the surrogate replaces a GEMM Y=XW (K*N FLOPs/row) with a rank-r map costing r*(K+N)+r^2 FLOPs/row — it is a FLOP-REDUCTION/throughput lever, not a utilization lever. MFU measures delivered FLOPs vs peak; (1) the low-rank ops are skinny GEMV-like memory-bound kernels, so silicon FLOP utilization would DROP, not rise (the rank report's realized-vs-ceiling gap makes this concrete: theoretical FLOP-ratio 56.7x, cuBLAS two-GEMM best-case only 3.6-11.7x, shipped kernel 0.04x — :27-29, :105 'the FLOP ceiling is not just unrealized, it is inverted'); (2) even tok/s-style 'effective MFU' (dense-FLOPs/wall-clock) cannot rise because at ranks where a speedup survives quality is unusable and at quality-surviving rank r~2048 the ceiling is only 1.8x (:23-26 verbatim: 'even a tensor-core-optimized kernel could not rescue the approach'); (3) it never fires anyway (OOD 0.96>>0.05). The scorecard's own G3 conclusion (batching is the MFU lever; the forward is non-GEMM-bound at ~68%) is orthogonal to and unaided by Koopman. Verdict: built-but-(correctly)-never-fires; NO credible path from this mechanism to an MFU lift — Goal-4's 'MFU' framing was a metric mismatch from the start.

Documented reconciling facts: (a) snapshot:66 itself files W6 as 'vLLM 0.21.0 cudagraph' grade-B prior, distinct from its own eager runs; snapshot:34 'cudagraph is 2.05× eager on this workload'; (b) the contaminated run's own counters show calls=0 handled=0 passthrough=0 (clean_bench3.err:3697) — the cost is per-launch observation overhead, and eager short-decode is launch-bound (R.A memo: eager-host tax +51%), maximally exposed to per-launch CPU work, whereas under cudagraph capture+replay the substrate's CUPTI launch callbacks/GOT interception are not on the per-step replay path and W6's much larger work-per-step further amortizes it (this mechanistic split is INFERENCE consistent with both reports — never directly profiled); (c) different substrate builds (259ac994 vs 2edba0d2) and load mechanisms, so W6 neutrality does not certify today's binary in eager passthrough. SOURCE-VS-REPORT TENSION worth flagging: current cipher_vllm_kv.py register() loads the substrate BEFORE the CIPHER_KV_ALLOC gate (:910 vs :913, added as 'W14-followup Step 0' referencing 2026-05-24, i.e., AFTER the W6 redo of 2026-05-23) — under today's plugin, W6's vanilla arm env (CIPHER_KV_ALLOC=0, W6:35) would NOT keep libcipher_rt out of the engine; only VLLM_PLUGINS="" does. W6's vanilla/CIPHER split is therefore only as clean as the 05-23-era plugin, which is not preserved for audit.
